summary: A solid, honest Stage 4 73 surface with exact key count, broad geometry, and a working synthesized basic voice. It falls well short of reference-level hardware density and responsive presentation, while the audio/input implementation has important untested lifecycle gaps. All four required technical checks pass.

criteria.label: Silhouette, chassis, and geometry
evidence: The sealed desktop capture shows one continuous red 73-key chassis that occupies about 94% of the 1440px viewport; the visual audit records the selected 3.095:1 73-key silhouette and 54/46 deck/keybed allocation.
src/App.tsx defines MIDI 28–100 (E1–E7) and renders 73 keys; its test asserts 73 accessible piano-key buttons and both endpoint names.
The end cheeks, rails, and deck detailing are materially simplified compared with the assigned product photo.

criteria.label: Complete hardware inventory and placement
evidence: All six ordered surface sections are present, with two primary OLEDs only in Program and Synth; the Organ has nine drawbars and LED ladders.

The implementation declares only 5 Performance controls, 15 Organ controls, 9 Piano controls, 18 Program controls, 18 Synth controls, and 16 Effects controls. The reference contains substantially denser and more differentiated physical groups, switches, faders, and landmarks.
The desktop capture visibly uses generic repeated control banks, especially across Piano, Synth, and Layer Effects, rather than closely placed reference-specific hardware.

criteria.label: Materials, color, typography, and displays
evidence: The capture has a credible red-metal chassis, dark blue-gray inset panels, black knobs, white/black keys, LED ladders, and blue-green OLED styling that align with the visual palette.
Much of the label text is extremely small or truncated, and the controls, display layouts, shadows, and panel typography are simplified relative to the product photo.

criteria.label: Narrow retention
evidence: The 390x844 capture keeps the instrument available through a 1060px-wide horizontal inspection canvas and includes an instruction to scroll horizontally.
At its captured initial position, most of the chassis and keybed are off-screen rather than retained in a responsive complete view; inspection requires horizontal scrolling.

criteria.label: Unified playable inputs
evidence: The implementation routes pointer down/up/cancel, computer keyboard mappings with repeat suppression, Space sustain, and MIDI note/velocity/CC64 to shared play/release/setPedal callbacks; blur performs all-notes-off.
MIDI permission denial/unavailability and disconnect status are exposed, but only inputs existing when access resolves receive onmidimessage handlers; a subsequently connected input is not bound.
The only automated input tests cover one pointer key and one keyboard/Space path; they do not exercise independent multitouch, MIDI messages, denial, reconnect, or blur cleanup.

criteria.label: Voice lifecycle and performance
evidence: PianoAudio supplies velocity-dependent envelopes, 16-voice oldest-first stealing, per-note release envelopes, sustain deferral, all-notes-off, and disposal of its AudioContext.

noteOff(note) releases every voice instance sharing that MIDI note. Releasing one of two overlapping same-note inputs therefore terminates both, so repeated/overlapping-note ownership is not dependable.
No test exercises audio output, velocity relationship, sustain duration, stealing, node cleanup, or overlapping same-note behavior.

criteria.label: Basic source and status honesty
evidence: IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json accurately declares live Web Audio triangle plus sine synthesis and explicitly says it is not a recorded sample set.
The visible status identifies a synthesized piano and reports MIDI unavailable, enabled, disconnected, or permission denied states.
AudioContext construction failure is silent: ensure() simply returns when no constructor exists, without an audio error/fallback status.

criteria.label: Control movement and feedback
evidence: Every rendered panel input is created from the stable id/label/kind/value model and renders as either a button with aria-pressed or a named range input; key buttons expose aria-pressed and pointer/keyboard handling.
Buttons light, knobs rotate visually, and faders/drawbars/wheels use native range controls with visible focus styling.

criteria.label: Decorative-control boundary
evidence: Panel interactions only update the normalized hardware presentation state. The audio path is only reached by keybed play/release and the dedicated sustain input.
The Program OLED explicitly says 'Panel controls decorative'; however, fixed Program/Synth screen content can still read as functional state even though no panel control changes it.

criteria.label: Data structure and tests
evidence: The section/control model provides stable IDs and a normalized presentation-state record, and PianoAudio separates core voice operations from the rendered controls.
Browser, audio, MIDI, and timing boundaries are not injectable; the single App.test.tsx has four UI-state tests only, although feature-matrix.json maps all 11 required feature IDs to it.
The tests do not provide the required behavioral evidence for multi-input lifecycle, audio signal behavior, MIDI failures, cleanup, or complete control inventory.

criteria.label: Runtime quality
evidence: I reran pnpm run test, typecheck, lint, and build against the sealed source; all passed (4/4 tests).
The sealed capture metadata reports no page errors at either canonical viewport. It does report the same nonstandard slider-vertical CSS warning at both viewports.
Source code installs blur/unmount cleanup and deterministic 16-voice handling, but the missing lifecycle coverage and horizontal narrow layout limit confidence under real stress.

issues: Reference hardware inventory and micro-layout are substantially reduced; several sections rely on generic control grids rather than the product's differentiated hardware.
Narrow presentation depends on horizontal scrolling, leaving the majority of the chassis outside the initial 390px capture.
Overlapping inputs for the same MIDI note are not independently owned: noteOff releases all voices for that note.
New MIDI inputs connected after access is granted do not receive a message handler.
Feature-matrix coverage is nominal rather than behavioral: four UI tests are mapped to all eleven Phase 1 feature IDs.
